source: Curated from public MedlinePlus, CDC, WHO, and NIH condition pages. English-only, adult-focused. Not a clinical reference — consumer education only.

diseases.name: Common Cold
diseases.description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat caused by several virus families, most commonly rhinoviruses. It spreads easily through droplets and shared surfaces, which is why colds are so common in autumn and winter. Typical symptoms include a runny or blocked nose, sneezing, mild cough and a low-grade fever, and most adults recover fully within 7-10 days without treatment. Rest, fluids and simple over-the-counter remedies are usually enough.
precautions: Avoid close contact with others while symptomatic
diets: Citrus fruits rich in vitamin C
redFlagHints: Mild fever, runny nose, sore throat, cough lasting under 10 days

diseases.name: Influenza (Flu)
diseases.description: Influenza is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza A and B viruses, typically peaking during cold months. Unlike a common cold it tends to come on suddenly, with high fever, body aches, fatigue and dry cough lasting five to seven days. Most healthy adults recover with rest and fluids, but older adults, pregnant women and people with chronic conditions can develop complications like pneumonia. Annual vaccination and early antiviral treatment within 48 hours significantly reduce severity.
workouts: Resume light activity only after fever resolves
redFlagHints: High fever (above 102°F), severe body aches, fatigue lasting 5-7 days, dry cough

diseases.name: COVID-19
diseases.description: COVID-19 is an illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus that primarily affects the respiratory system but can involve many organs. Symptoms range from mild (cough, loss of smell, sore throat) to severe (breathlessness, low oxygen, confusion), and risk of severe disease rises with age, obesity and chronic conditions. Most people recover at home within one to two weeks with rest and symptomatic care. Vaccination dramatically lowers the chance of hospitalisation, and antivirals like Paxlovid can help high-risk patients if started early.
redFlagHints: Loss of smell or taste, persistent cough, shortness of breath, low oxygen saturation

diseases.name: Pneumonia
diseases.description: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, causing them to fill with fluid or pus. It can be triggered by bacteria (most commonly Streptococcus pneumoniae), viruses or fungi, and often develops after a cold or flu. Typical signs include a productive cough, fever, chills, chest pain on deep breaths and breathlessness, and severity can range from mild and walk-around to life-threatening. Prompt antibiotics (for bacterial causes), supportive care and pneumococcal vaccination are the main lines of defence.
precautions: Complete full antibiotic course if prescribed
diets: Plenty of fluids to thin mucus
redFlagHints: Productive cough with green/yellow mucus, chest pain on deep breath, fever, breathlessness

diseases.name: Acute Bronchitis
diseases.description: Acute bronchitis is a short-lived inflammation of the bronchial tubes, the airways that carry air to the lungs. It almost always follows a viral cold or flu and features a persistent cough that starts dry and later produces mucus, often with mild chest discomfort and low-grade fever. Most cases resolve on their own within three weeks without antibiotics. Staying hydrated, avoiding tobacco smoke and using cough suppressants at night for sleep are usually enough to get through it.
workouts: Light walking once acute phase passes
redFlagHints: Persistent cough with mucus lasting 2-3 weeks after a cold

diseases.name: Chronic Bronchitis
diseases.description: Chronic bronchitis is a long-term form of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in which the airways are continuously inflamed and produce excess mucus. It is defined clinically by a productive cough present on most days for at least three months in two consecutive years. Smoking is by far the commonest cause, with air pollutants and occupational dust also contributing. Quitting smoking, inhaled bronchodilators, pulmonary rehabilitation and vaccination against flu and pneumococcus slow decline and reduce flare-ups.
redFlagHints: Smoker or ex-smoker, daily productive cough over months/years

diseases.name: Asthma
diseases.description: Asthma is a chronic condition in which the airways narrow, swell and produce extra mucus, making breathing difficult. Triggers include allergens (dust mites, pollen, pets), viral infections, cold air, exercise and emotional stress. Typical symptoms are wheezing, chest tightness, breathlessness and cough, often worse at night or early morning. Most people manage asthma well with a daily controller inhaler plus a rescue inhaler for flare-ups and by identifying and avoiding personal triggers.
workouts: Use inhaler before exercise if prescribed
redFlagHints: Wheezing, breathlessness worse at night or on exertion, dry cough, triggered by allergens

diseases.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
diseases.description: COPD is a progressive lung disease that limits airflow and makes breathing increasingly difficult over time. It is nearly always caused by long-term exposure to irritants — most commonly cigarette smoke — and results from chronic bronchitis, emphysema, or both. Key symptoms are breathlessness on exertion that worsens with years, a chronic cough and frequent chest infections. While there is no cure, quitting smoking, inhalers, pulmonary rehabilitation and vaccines can dramatically improve quality of life and slow progression.
precautions: Avoid air pollutants and respiratory infections
Get vaccinated against flu and pneumococcus
diets: Small frequent meals to reduce breathlessness
redFlagHints: Long smoking history, chronic breathlessness on exertion, barrel chest, productive cough

diseases.name: Tuberculosis
diseases.description: Tuberculosis is a potentially serious bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that most often affects the lungs. It spreads through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs, sneezes or speaks, especially in crowded or poorly ventilated settings. Classic features include a cough lasting more than three weeks, unintentional weight loss, drenching night sweats and low-grade fever. TB is fully curable with a supervised 6-month antibiotic regimen, and completing the full course is critical to prevent drug resistance.
precautions: Complete the full 6+ month antibiotic course
redFlagHints: Night sweats with unintentional weight loss, chronic cough (>3 weeks), low-grade fever

diseases.name: Sinusitis
diseases.description: Sinusitis is inflammation or infection of the sinus cavities in the face, usually triggered by a cold, allergic reaction or a structural issue like a deviated septum. It produces facial pressure or pain (especially over the forehead and cheeks), thick nasal discharge, reduced smell and sometimes a headache that worsens on bending forward. Most cases are viral and resolve within 10 days using saline rinses, steam inhalation and simple pain relief. Antibiotics are reserved for bacterial infections that last longer than 10 days or worsen after initial improvement.
diets: Avoid dairy if it thickens mucus
workouts: Gentle cardio once acute pain subsides
redFlagHints: Facial pain/pressure, nasal discharge, reduced smell, headache worse when bending forward

diseases.name: Pharyngitis
diseases.description: Pharyngitis is inflammation of the throat that causes pain, scratchiness and difficulty swallowing. Most cases are viral and clear up within a week with rest, warm fluids and lozenges. A smaller portion are caused by group A streptococcus (strep throat), which requires antibiotics to prevent complications like rheumatic fever. Warning signs that suggest strep include severe pain on swallowing, white patches on the tonsils, fever above 101°F and swollen lymph nodes in the neck.
precautions: Get tested for strep if symptoms severe
diets: Ice cream or cold drinks can soothe
redFlagHints: Severe sore throat, white patches or pus in throat, fever, swollen lymph nodes

diseases.name: Tonsillitis
diseases.description: Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils — the two oval pads at the back of the throat — most often caused by viruses but sometimes by bacteria. It presents with sore throat, painful swallowing, swollen tender glands in the neck and sometimes fever. Viral tonsillitis usually clears with supportive care and cool soft foods, while bacterial tonsillitis responds to a course of antibiotics. Recurrent severe tonsillitis may lead a specialist to recommend tonsillectomy.
redFlagHints: Severe pain on swallowing, enlarged tonsils with white patches, fever

diseases.name: Laryngitis
diseases.description: Laryngitis is inflammation of the voice box (larynx), most often from overuse, a cold, or irritants like smoke and alcohol. The hallmark symptom is hoarseness or complete voice loss, sometimes with a dry cough and mild sore throat. Acute laryngitis resolves within a week with voice rest, humidified air and adequate hydration. Hoarseness lasting more than three weeks should be evaluated by a doctor to rule out chronic irritation, reflux or other causes.
workouts: Avoid shouting or strenuous vocal use
redFlagHints: Hoarseness or voice loss, dry cough, mild sore throat

diseases.name: Pulmonary Embolism
diseases.description: A pulmonary embolism is a sudden blockage in a pulmonary artery, usually from a clot that has traveled from a deep vein in the leg. It is a life-threatening emergency because it can quickly reduce oxygen delivery to the body and strain the heart. Warning signs include sudden sharp chest pain worse with breathing, breathlessness, a rapid heart rate and sometimes fainting or coughing up blood. Immediate hospital evaluation with imaging and anticoagulant therapy is essential — survival depends on rapid recognition and treatment.
diets: Avoid foods that interact with anticoagulants
workouts: No exercise until cleared by physician
redFlagHints: Sudden sharp chest pain, breathlessness, rapid heart rate, leg swelling, recent immobilization

diseases.name: Pleurisy
diseases.description: Pleurisy is inflammation of the pleura, the two thin layers of tissue that line the lungs and chest wall. It produces a sharp, stabbing chest pain that worsens with deep breathing, coughing or sneezing. Common causes include viral infections, pneumonia, pulmonary embolism and autoimmune disease, so evaluating the underlying cause is important. Treatment focuses on the underlying condition and relieving pain with NSAIDs.
redFlagHints: Sharp chest pain worsening with deep breath or cough

diseases.name: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)
diseases.description: RSV is a very common respiratory virus that causes mild cold-like symptoms in most adults but can be severe in infants under one year and in older adults with chronic illness. Symptoms include runny nose, cough, wheezing and sometimes fever. In vulnerable patients it can progress to bronchiolitis or pneumonia and require hospitalisation for oxygen and fluids. Newer monoclonal antibody and vaccine options now exist for high-risk groups.
redFlagHints: Wheezing, cough, fever, breathlessness in infants or elderly

diseases.name: Gastroenteritis
diseases.description: Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and intestines, most often caused by viruses like norovirus or rotavirus and typically spread by contaminated food, water or close contact. It produces watery diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal cramps and sometimes a low-grade fever. Most healthy adults recover in 1-3 days with rest and oral rehydration solutions, which prevent dehydration. Seek medical care if diarrhoea contains blood, vomiting prevents any fluid intake or if signs of dehydration such as dizziness or very dark urine develop.
precautions: Prevent dehydration with oral rehydration salts
redFlagHints: Watery diarrhea, vomiting, low-grade fever, recent contact with sick person

diseases.name: Food Poisoning
diseases.description: Food poisoning is an acute illness that follows eating food or drink contaminated with bacteria, viruses, parasites or their toxins. Common culprits include improperly stored leftovers, undercooked meat or eggs, unclean street food and raw seafood. Typical symptoms start within hours to a day and include nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhoea and abdominal cramps. Most cases resolve in 1-3 days with fluid replacement, though certain bacterial infections need antibiotics and severe dehydration always warrants urgent medical care.
precautions: Seek care if unable to keep fluids down
diets: Clear fluids first, then bland foods
redFlagHints: Vomiting/diarrhea after suspect meal (street food, seafood, leftovers), abdominal cramps

diseases.name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
diseases.description: GERD is a chronic condition in which stomach acid repeatedly backs up into the oesophagus, causing burning chest pain (heartburn), sour regurgitation and sometimes a chronic cough. Risk factors include obesity, pregnancy, hiatal hernia, smoking and certain foods. Most people improve with lifestyle changes — avoiding large late meals, elevating the head of the bed and losing weight — combined with acid-reducing medications like proton pump inhibitors. Long-term untreated GERD can lead to oesophagitis and, rarely, changes in the oesophageal lining that raise cancer risk.
precautions: Avoid eating 2-3 hours before lying down
diets: Avoid spicy, fatty, citrus, chocolate, caffeine
redFlagHints: Heartburn worse after meals or lying down, sour taste, chronic cough at night

diseases.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
diseases.description: Peptic ulcers are open sores in the lining of the stomach or the first part of the small intestine, most often caused by Helicobacter pylori infection or long-term NSAID use. The classic symptom is burning upper abdominal pain, often worse on an empty stomach and relieved by eating or antacids. Complications include bleeding, perforation and obstruction, which are medical emergencies. Diagnosis is confirmed by endoscopy or H. pylori testing, and treatment combines acid suppression with targeted antibiotics when infection is present.
medications: H. pylori eradication therapy (triple or quadruple)
workouts: Avoid exercise on empty stomach with pain
redFlagHints: Burning upper abdominal pain, worse on empty stomach, black tarry stools (emergency)

diseases.name: Gastritis
diseases.description: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining, which can develop suddenly (acute) or build up over time (chronic). Common triggers are alcohol, NSAIDs, stress, bile reflux and Helicobacter pylori infection. It usually causes upper abdominal discomfort, nausea, early fullness after meals and sometimes vomiting. Treatment focuses on removing the trigger, acid suppression with proton pump inhibitors and eradicating H. pylori when present.
redFlagHints: Upper abdominal pain, nausea, loss of appetite, indigestion

diseases.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
diseases.description: IBS is a common functional bowel disorder causing recurrent abdominal pain linked to changes in bowel habit — diarrhoea, constipation or alternating patterns — without any structural damage. Symptoms are often triggered by certain foods, stress or hormonal changes. While the exact cause isn't fully understood, a combination of gut hypersensitivity, motility changes and gut-brain signaling is involved. Most patients find relief through dietary changes (such as the low-FODMAP diet), stress management and targeted medications for the dominant symptom.
redFlagHints: Recurrent abdominal pain with bowel changes, bloating, no weight loss

diseases.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD)
diseases.description: IBD encompasses Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis — chronic autoimmune conditions that cause inflammation of the digestive tract. Symptoms include recurrent diarrhoea (sometimes bloody), abdominal pain, fatigue and unintentional weight loss, and can flare and remit over years. Uncontrolled inflammation can lead to serious complications like strictures, fistulas and bowel cancer, so close specialist follow-up is essential. Modern treatment ranges from 5-ASA drugs and steroids for mild disease to immunomodulators and biologics for moderate-to-severe cases.
workouts: Regular moderate exercise when in remission
redFlagHints: Chronic diarrhea (sometimes bloody), weight loss, abdominal pain, fatigue

diseases.name: Appendicitis
diseases.description: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix, a small pouch attached to the large intestine, and it is a surgical emergency. The classic pattern is pain starting around the belly button that shifts to the right lower abdomen within 12-24 hours, along with nausea, loss of appetite and low-grade fever. Without treatment the appendix can rupture, causing peritonitis, a serious infection of the abdominal cavity. Treatment is usually urgent surgical removal (appendectomy), though selected cases can be managed with antibiotics alone.
precautions: Do not use laxatives or heating pads
diets: Gradual return to solids after surgery
workouts: No exercise until cleared after surgery
redFlagHints: Pain starting near navel, moving to right lower abdomen, nausea, low-grade fever

diseases.name: Cholecystitis
diseases.description: Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder, most often from a gallstone obstructing the cystic duct. It typically causes severe right-upper-abdominal pain that may radiate to the right shoulder, nausea, vomiting and fever, often triggered by a fatty meal. Untreated cases can progress to infection, gangrene or perforation of the gallbladder. Treatment usually involves antibiotics, pain control and laparoscopic removal of the gallbladder within days of the acute episode.
precautions: Seek evaluation for right-upper abdominal pain
redFlagHints: Right-upper abdominal pain after fatty meals, nausea, fever

diseases.name: Hepatitis A
diseases.description: Hepatitis A is a highly contagious liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus, spread through food or water contaminated with infected faeces. Symptoms appear 2-6 weeks after exposure and include fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, jaundice and dark urine. Unlike hepatitis B and C it does not become chronic, and most people recover fully within a few weeks to months. A safe effective vaccine is available and widely recommended for travelers and people in outbreak areas.
medications: Supportive care only; no specific antiviral
redFlagHints: Jaundice, fatigue, nausea, dark urine, recent travel or food exposure

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.description: Hepatitis B is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus, spread through blood, unprotected sex, shared needles and from mother to baby at birth. Acute infection may cause fatigue, jaundice and abdominal pain, while many people develop chronic infection that silently damages the liver over decades, raising risk of cirrhosis and liver cancer. Safe effective vaccination provides lifelong protection and is recommended for all infants and at-risk adults. Chronic cases are managed with antiviral drugs that suppress the virus and reduce complications.
precautions: Avoid unsafe needles, unprotected sex, sharing razors
redFlagHints: Jaundice, fatigue, abdominal pain, history of unprotected contact or transfusion

diseases.name: Hepatitis C
diseases.description: Hepatitis C is a bloodborne viral infection of the liver that spreads mainly through shared needles, unscreened transfusions and, less commonly, unprotected sex. Most people have no symptoms for years, so screening is crucial in at-risk groups, since chronic infection can quietly lead to cirrhosis and liver cancer over decades. Unlike hepatitis B, there is no vaccine, but modern direct-acting antiviral medications cure more than 95% of cases with an 8-12 week oral course. Early diagnosis and treatment prevent the long-term complications.
precautions: Get tested if risk factors present
redFlagHints: Often asymptomatic, fatigue, possible mild jaundice, risk factors for bloodborne exposure

diseases.name: Jaundice
diseases.description: Jaundice is not a disease itself but a sign of an underlying problem, recognised by yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes from excess bilirubin in the blood. Causes range from liver infections (hepatitis), bile duct obstruction (gallstones, tumors) and excessive red blood cell breakdown (haemolysis) to certain medications. Accompanying clues like dark urine, pale stools, itching or abdominal pain point toward the cause. Any new jaundice warrants prompt medical evaluation with liver tests and imaging.
precautions: Seek prompt medical evaluation to identify cause
redFlagHints: Yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stool, itching

diseases.name: Pancreatitis
diseases.description: Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas, an organ that makes digestive enzymes and insulin. The two most common triggers are gallstones and heavy alcohol use, but high triglycerides, certain drugs and infections also cause it. Symptoms include severe upper-abdominal pain that often radiates to the back, nausea, vomiting and fever, and severe cases can progress to organ failure. Treatment involves hospital admission for IV fluids, pain control, removing the trigger and monitoring for complications.
precautions: Seek urgent care for severe abdominal pain
diets: Nothing by mouth during acute phase
redFlagHints: Severe upper abdominal pain radiating to back, nausea, vomiting, recent heavy alcohol

diseases.name: Constipation
diseases.description: Constipation describes infrequent bowel movements, hard stools or difficult passage, usually defined as fewer than three stools a week or persistent straining. Common causes include low-fibre diets, inadequate fluids, inactivity, ignoring the urge to go, medications and some hormonal conditions. Most cases respond well to lifestyle changes like increasing fibre gradually, drinking more water, regular exercise and fixed toilet times. Persistent or worsening constipation, especially with weight loss or blood in stool, needs medical evaluation to rule out structural causes.
workouts: Yoga poses that promote gut motility
redFlagHints: Infrequent stools, hard stools, straining, bloating

diseases.name: Hemorrhoids
diseases.description: Hemorrhoids are swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus that can cause itching, discomfort and painless bright-red bleeding with bowel movements. They're extremely common, especially during pregnancy and with chronic constipation, heavy lifting or prolonged sitting. Most mild cases improve with high-fibre diet, adequate fluids, warm sitz baths and topical creams. Larger or thrombosed hemorrhoids may require office procedures or, rarely, surgery.
precautions: Don't sit on toilet too long
diets: Avoid spicy foods if they aggravate
redFlagHints: Painless rectal bleeding, itching, swelling around anus

diseases.name: Diverticulitis
diseases.description: Diverticulitis occurs when small pouches (diverticula) that form in the colon wall become inflamed or infected. It most commonly presents after age 50 with left lower abdominal pain, fever and a change in bowel habits. Mild episodes can often be treated at home with clear fluids and oral antibiotics, while severe cases may need hospitalisation for IV antibiotics or surgery. Long-term prevention focuses on a high-fibre diet and avoiding smoking.
diets: Clear liquid diet during acute flare
redFlagHints: Left lower abdominal pain, fever, change in bowel habits, over age 50

diseases.name: Hypertension
diseases.description: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is persistently elevated pressure in the arteries, generally 130/80 mmHg or higher. It is often called a silent disease because it typically causes no symptoms until it has damaged the heart, kidneys, brain or eyes. Major risk factors include obesity, high-salt diet, physical inactivity, excess alcohol and family history. Regular monitoring, weight control, a low-salt DASH-style diet and — when needed — medications like ACE inhibitors or diuretics significantly reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
redFlagHints: Often silent; sometimes headaches, nosebleeds, dizziness when severe

diseases.name: Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack)
diseases.description: A heart attack occurs when blood flow to part of the heart muscle is blocked long enough for the tissue to start dying, usually because of a ruptured cholesterol plaque in a coronary artery. Classic warning signs include pressure-like chest pain that may radiate to the left arm or jaw, sweating, nausea and breathlessness, though women and diabetics often present atypically. Every minute of delay means more heart muscle lost, so call emergency services immediately at the first suspicion. Early clot-busting drugs or emergency angioplasty can save significant amounts of heart muscle.
precautions: Do not drive yourself to hospital
diets: Limit saturated fat, salt, added sugar
workouts: Gradual return to aerobic exercise under supervision
redFlagHints: Pressure/squeezing chest pain, radiating to arm/jaw, sweating, nausea, exertional trigger

diseases.name: Angina Pectoris
diseases.description: Angina is chest pain or pressure that comes from reduced blood flow to the heart, usually due to narrowed coronary arteries. Stable angina is triggered predictably by exertion or emotional stress and relieved by rest or nitroglycerin, while unstable angina occurs unpredictably, even at rest, and is a warning sign for a possible heart attack. Management combines lifestyle changes, anti-anginal medication (beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, nitrates), aggressive risk-factor control and — for some patients — stents or bypass surgery.
diets: Plenty of vegetables and whole grains
workouts: Gradual conditioning program under medical guidance
redFlagHints: Pressure-like chest discomfort on exertion, relieved by rest or nitroglycerin

diseases.name: Heart Failure
diseases.description: Heart failure is a chronic condition in which the heart cannot pump blood efficiently enough to meet the body's needs. It develops from coronary artery disease, long-standing hypertension, valve problems or prior heart attacks. Typical symptoms include breathlessness on exertion or lying flat, swelling in the ankles, unexplained fatigue and weight gain from fluid retention. Modern therapy — ACE inhibitors/ARNI, beta-blockers, SGLT2 inhibitors and diuretics combined with salt restriction and daily weight tracking — significantly extends life and reduces hospitalisations.
redFlagHints: Breathlessness on exertion or lying flat, leg swelling, fatigue, weight gain

diseases.name: Atrial Fibrillation
diseases.description: Atrial fibrillation (AFib) is an irregular and often rapid heart rhythm caused by chaotic electrical activity in the upper chambers of the heart. It increases the risk of stroke five-fold because blood can pool and clot in the atria. Common triggers and causes include hypertension, heart failure, thyroid disease and heavy alcohol use. Treatment focuses on controlling the heart rate or restoring normal rhythm, and — most importantly — preventing strokes with anticoagulants in patients whose risk score justifies it.
diets: Consistent vitamin K if on warfarin
redFlagHints: Irregular pulse, palpitations, fatigue, breathlessness

diseases.name: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
diseases.description: Deep vein thrombosis is a blood clot that forms in a deep vein, most commonly in the leg. It typically presents with unilateral leg swelling, calf pain or tenderness and warmth of the affected limb. Major risks include prolonged immobility (long flights, surgery, hospitalisation), pregnancy, cancer and certain clotting disorders. Untreated DVTs can break off and travel to the lungs, causing a life-threatening pulmonary embolism, so prompt anticoagulation with heparin or DOACs is essential.
diets: Consistent vitamin K intake if on warfarin
redFlagHints: Unilateral leg swelling, calf pain or tenderness, warmth, recent surgery or long travel

diseases.name: Aortic Dissection
diseases.description: Aortic dissection is a tear in the inner wall of the aorta, the large artery carrying blood from the heart, allowing blood to force the layers apart. It is a surgical emergency with high mortality if not recognised and treated quickly. The classic symptom is sudden severe tearing or ripping chest or back pain, sometimes with pulse differences between the two arms or signs of stroke. Rapid imaging (CT angiography) and urgent surgical or medical management of blood pressure are critical.
redFlagHints: Sudden severe tearing chest or back pain, pulse differences between arms

diseases.name: Pericarditis
diseases.description: Pericarditis is inflammation of the pericardium, the thin sac that surrounds the heart, most often following a viral infection. It typically produces sharp chest pain that worsens when lying flat and improves when sitting forward, and may be accompanied by low-grade fever. Most cases are self-limited and respond to NSAIDs or colchicine over several weeks. Complications like pericardial effusion or cardiac tamponade are uncommon but require urgent care.
redFlagHints: Sharp chest pain worse lying flat and better sitting forward

diseases.name: Ischemic Stroke
diseases.description: An ischemic stroke occurs when a blood clot or narrowed artery blocks blood flow to part of the brain, starving brain cells of oxygen. Every minute without blood flow destroys about two million neurons, so the phrase 'time is brain' guides treatment. Warning signs follow the BE-FAST pattern — balance loss, eye changes, face droop, arm weakness, speech difficulty and time to call emergency services. IV clot-busters within 4.5 hours and mechanical thrombectomy for large clots can restore function and limit disability.
precautions: Call emergency services immediately (time is brain)
redFlagHints: Sudden face droop, arm weakness, speech difficulty, vision changes

diseases.name: Hemorrhagic Stroke
diseases.description: A hemorrhagic stroke is bleeding into or around the brain, most commonly from a ruptured small vessel damaged by chronic hypertension, or from an aneurysm. Classic features include sudden severe headache, nausea, loss of consciousness and rapidly-progressing neurological deficits. Early emergency-department care focuses on controlling blood pressure, reversing any anticoagulation and urgently imaging the brain to decide if neurosurgical intervention is needed. Rehabilitation plays a central role in the long recovery.
redFlagHints: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, neurological deficits, high blood pressure

diseases.name: Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)
diseases.description: A transient ischemic attack is a temporary interruption of blood flow to the brain that produces stroke-like symptoms, which resolve within minutes to a few hours. While the episode itself passes, it is a major warning — about 1 in 10 people who have a TIA will have a full stroke within 90 days, many in the first few days. Urgent evaluation with imaging, cardiac monitoring and aggressive risk-factor control can dramatically reduce that risk. Antiplatelet drugs, statins and blood pressure control form the backbone of prevention.
redFlagHints: Temporary face droop, weakness, speech difficulty lasting minutes to hours

diseases.name: Postural Hypotension
diseases.description: Postural (orthostatic) hypotension is a drop in blood pressure of 20/10 mmHg or more within three minutes of standing, causing dizziness or lightheadedness. It is common in older adults, those with diabetes or Parkinson's disease, and anyone dehydrated or on blood-pressure medications. Practical strategies — rising slowly, wearing compression stockings, increasing fluid intake, avoiding hot showers — often help. Persistent symptoms may require reviewing medications or starting drugs like fludrocortisone or midodrine.
medications: Fludrocortisone or midodrine in severe cases
redFlagHints: Dizziness or lightheadedness on standing, often in older adults

diseases.name: Hyperlipidemia
diseases.description: Hyperlipidemia means elevated levels of cholesterol or triglycerides in the blood, which accelerate atherosclerosis and raise risk of heart attack and stroke. It is usually silent, detected on routine lipid screening triggered by age, family history or other risk factors. Lifestyle changes — a Mediterranean-style diet, regular exercise, weight control and quitting smoking — are first-line, with statins and newer agents added when targets are not reached. Routine lipid panels track progress and guide therapy.
redFlagHints: Often asymptomatic; detected via lipid panel

diseases.name: Migraine
diseases.description: Migraine is a recurrent neurological disorder that causes moderate-to-severe throbbing headaches, often on one side, lasting 4-72 hours. Common features include nausea, vomiting and sensitivity to light and sound, and about one in three sufferers experience aura (visual zigzags, tingling, speech changes) beforehand. Triggers vary by person and include specific foods, hormonal changes, lack of sleep and stress. Modern treatment combines acute relief (triptans, NSAIDs, gepants) with preventive therapy (CGRP inhibitors, beta-blockers, topiramate) when attacks are frequent.
diets: Avoid personal triggers (aged cheese, wine, MSG)
redFlagHints: Throbbing one-sided headache, nausea, light sensitivity, sometimes visual aura

diseases.name: Tension-Type Headache
diseases.description: Tension-type headache is the most common type of headache, described as a dull pressure or tight band around the head affecting both sides. It typically builds gradually and lasts hours to days, often worse toward the end of the workday. Contributors include stress, poor posture, lack of sleep and eye strain, and the headache is usually milder than migraine and not associated with nausea. Most cases respond to over-the-counter analgesics, good sleep, stress-reduction techniques and regular aerobic exercise.
redFlagHints: Mild to moderate bilateral pressure headache without nausea

diseases.name: Cluster Headache
diseases.description: Cluster headaches are among the most painful headaches known, striking as sudden severe one-sided attacks around the eye or temple lasting 15 minutes to three hours. Accompanying symptoms include tearing, nasal congestion or a drooping eyelid on the affected side, and attacks often come in 'clusters' of daily episodes over weeks, then remit. Men are more commonly affected and alcohol is a classic trigger during a cluster period. Acute treatment is high-flow oxygen or subcutaneous sumatriptan; verapamil helps prevent attacks.
redFlagHints: Severe one-sided eye pain with tearing, congestion, agitation

diseases.name: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
diseases.description: Subarachnoid hemorrhage is bleeding into the space between the brain and its protective membranes, most often from a ruptured brain aneurysm. The hallmark is a sudden 'thunderclap' — the worst headache of the person's life — reaching peak intensity within seconds, often with vomiting, neck stiffness, light sensitivity or brief loss of consciousness. Without rapid diagnosis by CT scan and urgent neurosurgical or endovascular treatment, mortality is very high. Any unusually severe sudden-onset headache should be treated as an emergency.
redFlagHints: Sudden 'thunderclap' worst-ever headache, vomiting, neck stiffness, loss of consciousness

diseases.name: Bacterial Meningitis
diseases.description: Bacterial meningitis is a life-threatening infection of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, most commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis or Haemophilus influenzae. The classic triad is severe headache with fever and neck stiffness, often accompanied by light sensitivity, vomiting, rash and confusion. Every hour of delay significantly worsens outcomes, so immediate IV antibiotics and dexamethasone are started even before lab confirmation. Vaccination against meningococcal, pneumococcal and Hib organisms has greatly reduced incidence.
redFlagHints: Severe headache with fever, neck stiffness, light sensitivity, rash, altered mental status

diseases.name: Viral Encephalitis
diseases.description: Viral encephalitis is inflammation of the brain tissue itself, most often caused by herpes simplex virus but also by arboviruses (e.g., Japanese encephalitis) and others. Symptoms range from mild flu-like illness to severe neurological impairment — fever with confusion, altered personality, seizures or focal weakness are all warning signs. Diagnosis is urgent and involves MRI, lumbar puncture and PCR testing; empiric acyclovir is usually started immediately pending results. Recovery is often incomplete and cognitive rehabilitation may be needed.
redFlagHints: Fever with confusion, seizures, personality changes, focal deficits

diseases.name: Epilepsy
diseases.description: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterised by recurrent unprovoked seizures due to abnormal bursts of electrical activity in the brain. Seizures can range from brief staring spells (absence) to generalised convulsions with loss of consciousness. Causes include prior brain injury, stroke, brain tumors and genetic factors, but in many patients no cause is identified. Most people achieve good seizure control with a single antiseizure medication, and lifestyle measures — consistent sleep, avoiding alcohol, medication adherence — are crucial.
diets: Ketogenic diet in select refractory cases
workouts: Most activities are safe with controlled seizures
redFlagHints: Recurrent convulsions, staring spells, or brief loss of awareness

diseases.name: Bell's Palsy
diseases.description: Bell's palsy is a sudden, typically unilateral weakness or paralysis of the muscles of the face, caused by inflammation of the facial nerve. The cause is often linked to reactivation of herpes simplex virus, and onset is rapid — frequently overnight. Most people recover fully within three to six months, and early treatment (within 72 hours) with oral corticosteroids improves recovery rates. Protecting the affected eye with artificial tears and a patch at night prevents corneal damage during the weakness phase.
precautions: Protect affected eye (artificial tears, eye patch at night)
Seek evaluation for sudden facial weakness
redFlagHints: Sudden unilateral face droop, usually without limb weakness or speech change

diseases.name: Multiple Sclerosis
diseases.description: Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the protective myelin sheath around nerve fibers in the brain and spinal cord. This disrupts signals and produces episodic neurological symptoms — vision changes, weakness, numbness, fatigue, balance problems — that can remit and relapse. It most commonly affects adults 20-40 and is more common in women. Modern disease-modifying therapies have dramatically changed prognosis, reducing relapse rates and slowing disability progression.
redFlagHints: Episodic neurological symptoms (vision, weakness, numbness) in young adults

diseases.name: Parkinson's Disease
diseases.description: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurological disorder caused by loss of dopamine-producing brain cells in the substantia nigra. The cardinal features are resting tremor, muscle rigidity, slow movement (bradykinesia) and postural instability, often preceded by years of subtle signs like reduced smell and REM sleep behaviour disorder. Symptoms are well controlled for many years with levodopa-based medication, dopamine agonists and physical therapy. Deep brain stimulation is a valuable option for advanced disease with significant motor fluctuations.
redFlagHints: Resting tremor, slowness, stiffness, small handwriting

diseases.name: Peripheral Neuropathy
diseases.description: Peripheral neuropathy is damage to the peripheral nerves, producing numbness, tingling, burning pain or weakness — most commonly in a stocking-glove pattern in the hands and feet. The most frequent causes are diabetes, vitamin B12 deficiency, heavy alcohol use, chemotherapy and certain autoimmune diseases. Treatment addresses the underlying cause and manages pain with agents like gabapentin, pregabalin or duloxetine. Daily foot care is particularly important for diabetics because loss of sensation raises the risk of unnoticed injuries and ulcers.
precautions: Identify and treat underlying cause (diabetes, B12 deficiency)
redFlagHints: Numbness/tingling/pain in hands or feet, often symmetric, often in diabetics

diseases.name: Dengue Fever
diseases.description: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, common in tropical and subtropical regions. It typically causes sudden high fever, intense headache, severe body and joint aches (sometimes called 'breakbone fever'), retro-orbital eye pain and a rash. A small portion of patients develop severe dengue with warning signs like abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding and plasma leakage that require urgent hospital care. Treatment is supportive with fluids and paracetamol — aspirin and NSAIDs should be avoided because of bleeding risk.
diets: Plenty of fluids (ORS, papaya leaf in tradition)
redFlagHints: High fever 2-7 days, severe body aches, retro-orbital pain, recent travel to dengue-endemic area

diseases.name: Malaria
diseases.description: Malaria is a mosquito-borne parasitic infection caused by Plasmodium species, with falciparum being the most dangerous. Typical presentation is cyclic fevers with chills and sweating, often with headache, body aches and fatigue, appearing one to several weeks after travel or residence in endemic areas. Severe malaria can cause cerebral complications, kidney failure and death, especially in children and pregnant women. Artemisinin-based combination therapy is first-line, and prevention relies on mosquito-avoidance measures and, where appropriate, chemoprophylaxis during travel.
redFlagHints: Cyclic fevers with chills and sweats, travel or residence in malaria-endemic area

diseases.name: Typhoid Fever
diseases.description: Typhoid fever is a systemic bacterial infection by Salmonella typhi, spread through food and water contaminated with faeces from an infected person. It presents with progressive stepwise fever over several days, abdominal pain, either constipation or diarrhoea, relative bradycardia and sometimes a rose-coloured rash on the trunk. Without antibiotics, up to 20% of cases develop serious complications like intestinal perforation. Early diagnosis, appropriate antibiotics (azithromycin, ceftriaxone or fluoroquinolones where sensitive) and good food and water hygiene are key.
redFlagHints: Progressive fever over days, abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhea, relative bradycardia

diseases.name: Cholera
diseases.description: Cholera is an acute diarrhoeal illness caused by Vibrio cholerae, acquired mainly from contaminated water or food in areas with poor sanitation. The illness produces sudden profuse painless watery diarrhoea — often described as 'rice-water' — with rapid onset of severe dehydration within hours. Aggressive oral rehydration, and IV fluids when severe, are life-saving; many patients who reach treatment quickly make full recoveries. Vaccination is available for travelers and in outbreak response.
redFlagHints: Profuse watery 'rice-water' diarrhea, rapid dehydration, outbreak area

diseases.name: Chikungunya
diseases.description: Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral infection caused by an alphavirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, common in tropical regions. It produces sudden high fever with severe joint pain that often persists for weeks or months after the acute illness. Other features include headache, muscle pain, nausea and a rash. Treatment is supportive with rest, fluids and paracetamol, and mosquito-avoidance measures prevent transmission.
medications: Acetaminophen (avoid NSAIDs early until dengue excluded)
redFlagHints: Sudden fever with severe joint pain, endemic area exposure

diseases.name: Measles
diseases.description: Measles is a highly contagious viral illness that spreads through respiratory droplets, and unvaccinated people of any age are at risk. The characteristic pattern is three days of fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes followed by a maculopapular rash starting on the face and spreading downward. Complications include pneumonia, ear infection and, rarely, encephalitis, and measles remains a major cause of child mortality globally. Two doses of the MMR vaccine provide lifelong protection and are the cornerstone of prevention.
precautions: Vitamin A supplementation in deficient regions
redFlagHints: Fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, maculopapular rash starting on face

diseases.name: Chickenpox
diseases.description: Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral illness caused by varicella-zoster virus, producing an itchy rash of fluid-filled blisters that crust over in stages. It is typically mild in children but can be severe in adults and immunocompromised patients. After the initial illness the virus stays dormant in nerve ganglia and can reactivate years later as shingles. Routine childhood varicella vaccination has dramatically reduced cases in countries where it is standard.
diets: Soft cool foods if mouth sores
redFlagHints: Fever with widespread itchy blistering rash at various stages

diseases.name: Mumps
diseases.description: Mumps is a viral infection that classically causes painful swelling of one or both parotid salivary glands, along with fever, headache, fatigue and loss of appetite. It spreads through respiratory droplets and close contact, and most cases resolve in about a week. Complications — more common in adults — include orchitis in post-pubertal males, meningitis and hearing loss. Two doses of the MMR vaccine provide strong, lasting protection.
diets: Avoid acidic foods that trigger saliva
redFlagHints: Painful swelling of cheeks/jaw, fever, headache, fatigue

diseases.name: Rubella
diseases.description: Rubella (German measles) is typically a mild viral illness in children and adults, producing a low-grade fever, swollen lymph nodes behind the ears and a fine pink rash spreading from the face. Its importance lies in its severe consequences during pregnancy — infection in the first trimester can cause congenital rubella syndrome with cardiac defects, deafness and cataracts in the baby. Universal MMR vaccination has eliminated endemic transmission in many countries. Pregnant women who haven't been vaccinated should avoid anyone suspected of having rubella.
redFlagHints: Mild fever with fine pink rash spreading from face, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy

diseases.name: HIV/AIDS
diseases.description: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) attacks CD4 T-cells, progressively weakening the immune system; untreated it can progress over years to AIDS, defined by severe immune suppression and opportunistic infections. It spreads through unprotected sex, sharing needles and mother-to-child during birth or breastfeeding. Modern antiretroviral therapy (ART) suppresses the virus to undetectable levels, protects the immune system and prevents transmission to partners. Early testing, daily ART and routine monitoring allow people living with HIV to have near-normal life expectancy.
workouts: Regular moderate exercise supports immune function
redFlagHints: Recurrent infections, unexplained weight loss, night sweats, risk exposure

diseases.name: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease
diseases.description: Hand, foot and mouth disease is a common viral illness in children under five, caused by enteroviruses such as coxsackievirus A16. It produces painful mouth ulcers, fever and a typical blister-like rash on the palms and soles, sometimes on the buttocks. It spreads easily in daycare and school settings, and most children recover within 7-10 days with rest, fluids and pain relief. Adults occasionally get it, usually with milder symptoms.
redFlagHints: Mouth sores with rash on palms and soles in children

diseases.name: Leptospirosis
diseases.description: Leptospirosis is a bacterial infection transmitted through water or soil contaminated with urine from infected animals, especially rats. It often spikes after floods and monsoon rains, and presents with sudden high fever, severe muscle aches (especially in the calves), headache, red eyes and jaundice. Severe cases (Weil's disease) cause liver failure, kidney injury and bleeding. Early doxycycline or penicillin is effective, and prevention involves avoiding contact with contaminated water and covering skin wounds.
precautions: Cover cuts when in flooded areas
redFlagHints: High fever, severe muscle pain (calves), red eyes, jaundice after flood/water exposure

diseases.name: Rabies
diseases.description: Rabies is a viral infection of the nervous system transmitted through bites or scratches from infected mammals, most commonly dogs in low-income regions and bats in high-income ones. Once symptoms appear — hydrophobia, agitation, paralysis — the disease is almost universally fatal. Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) with rabies immunoglobulin plus a four-dose vaccine series is nearly 100% effective if started promptly after an exposure. Any bite from an unknown animal should be washed thoroughly and assessed urgently.
medications: Rabies immunoglobulin + vaccine series after exposure
redFlagHints: Recent animal bite, later progressive neurological symptoms

diseases.name: Scrub Typhus
diseases.description: Scrub typhus is a bacterial infection caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, transmitted through the bite of chigger mites found in scrub vegetation. It presents with fever, severe headache, myalgia and a characteristic painless black ulcer (eschar) at the bite site, often with regional lymph node enlargement and a rash. Untreated cases can progress to severe multiorgan involvement. Doxycycline or azithromycin are the treatments of choice and produce rapid improvement.
precautions: Use insect repellents in endemic areas
Wear long clothing in tall grass
diets: Adequate fluids and nutrition during illness
redFlagHints: Fever with headache, rash, and characteristic black eschar, rural area exposure

diseases.name: Lyme Disease
diseases.description: Lyme disease is caused by the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi, transmitted by the bite of certain ticks in wooded areas of North America and Europe. Early disease features an expanding 'bullseye' rash (erythema migrans) around the bite site, often with fever, fatigue and joint aches. If untreated, later stages can involve arthritis, neurological and cardiac complications. A short course of oral doxycycline or amoxicillin cures most cases when started early; prevention focuses on tick checks and permethrin-treated clothing.
redFlagHints: Expanding bullseye rash after tick bite, fever, fatigue, joint pain

diseases.name: Infectious Mononucleosis
diseases.description: Infectious mononucleosis, commonly called mono, is caused by Epstein-Barr virus and typically affects teens and young adults. The classic presentation is prolonged sore throat, high fever, extreme fatigue and widespread lymph node swelling, often with an enlarged spleen. Because of the spleen enlargement, contact sports and heavy lifting should be avoided for 4-6 weeks to prevent rupture. Treatment is supportive; antibiotics (especially ampicillin) should be avoided because they commonly cause a rash in mono.
precautions: Avoid contact sports for 4-6 weeks (spleen rupture risk)
diets: Cool soft foods if sore throat
redFlagHints: Prolonged sore throat, fatigue, fever, swollen lymph nodes in young adult

diseases.name: Norovirus Gastroenteritis
diseases.description: Norovirus is a highly contagious virus and the leading cause of outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis, notorious on cruise ships and in schools, nursing homes and restaurants. It causes the abrupt onset of vomiting and watery diarrhoea, usually lasting 24-72 hours. Strict hand hygiene with soap and water (alcohol gels are less effective) and surface disinfection with bleach are key to limiting spread. Treatment is supportive with oral rehydration.
precautions: Strict hand hygiene (soap and water, alcohol gel less effective)
diets: Clear fluids first, bland foods after
redFlagHints: Sudden onset vomiting and diarrhea, outbreak at workplace/school/cruise

diseases.name: Yellow Fever
diseases.description: Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne viral hemorrhagic fever prevalent in parts of Africa and South America. Many cases are mild with fever and body aches, but a severe 'toxic' phase can develop with jaundice, bleeding and multi-organ failure. There is no specific antiviral treatment, so supportive care is the mainstay. A single dose of the yellow fever vaccine provides lifelong protection and is required for travel to many endemic countries.
precautions: Vaccine before travel to endemic areas
redFlagHints: Fever, jaundice, bleeding after travel to endemic area

diseases.name: Zika Virus Infection
diseases.description: Zika is a mosquito-borne viral infection, usually mild in adults with symptoms such as low-grade fever, fine rash, conjunctivitis and joint pain for about a week. Its major concern is in pregnancy — infection can cause microcephaly and other severe birth defects in the fetus. Sexual transmission is also possible, so couples planning pregnancy should take precautions after travel to endemic areas. Prevention relies on mosquito-avoidance measures and condom use.
precautions: Avoid travel to outbreak areas during pregnancy
redFlagHints: Mild fever, rash, red eyes, joint pain after travel to endemic area

diseases.name: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
diseases.description: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition in which the pancreas produces little or no insulin, typically starting in childhood or young adulthood. Classic symptoms are rapid-onset increased thirst, frequent urination, unintended weight loss and fatigue, and untreated the condition can progress to diabetic ketoacidosis, a medical emergency. Lifelong insulin therapy — increasingly via insulin pumps paired with continuous glucose monitors — is required. Good glycemic control delays or prevents long-term complications affecting eyes, kidneys and nerves.
workouts: Regular exercise with careful glucose monitoring
redFlagHints: New onset thirst, frequent urination, weight loss, usually younger age

diseases.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
diseases.description: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic metabolic disorder characterised by insulin resistance and progressive insulin deficiency, with strong ties to obesity, inactivity and genetic predisposition. Many patients are asymptomatic and diagnosed only by screening, while others present with fatigue, thirst, frequent urination or blurred vision. Lifestyle modification — weight loss, regular activity, balanced diet — is the foundation of treatment, supported by medications like metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 agonists. Tight control reduces risk of heart disease, stroke, kidney disease and nerve damage.
diets: Limit sugary drinks and refined carbs
redFlagHints: Thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, blurred vision, often overweight adult

diseases.name: Hypoglycemia
diseases.description: Hypoglycemia means abnormally low blood glucose, typically below 70 mg/dL, and is most commonly seen in diabetics treated with insulin or sulfonylureas. Early symptoms are adrenergic — sweating, shakiness, palpitations and hunger — while lower levels produce confusion, slurred speech and, if untreated, loss of consciousness and seizures. The 'rule of 15' — consuming 15g of fast-acting carbohydrate and rechecking in 15 minutes — is the standard immediate treatment. Recurrent episodes need review of diabetes medications and meal timing.
workouts: Monitor glucose before and after exercise
redFlagHints: Sweating, shakiness, palpitations, confusion, hunger, often in treated diabetics

diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism
diseases.description: Hyperthyroidism is an overactive thyroid gland producing excess thyroid hormone, most commonly from autoimmune Graves' disease or a toxic nodule. Typical features include weight loss despite a good appetite, palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, anxiety and — in Graves' — bulging eyes. Untreated hyperthyroidism increases cardiovascular risk and can trigger a life-threatening thyroid storm. Treatment options include antithyroid drugs (methimazole), radioactive iodine and surgery, with beta-blockers used for symptom control.
redFlagHints: Weight loss despite appetite, palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, bulging eyes

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
diseases.description: Hypothyroidism is an underactive thyroid gland that fails to produce enough thyroid hormone, most commonly from autoimmune Hashimoto's thyroiditis. It causes fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation and slow mental processing, symptoms that often develop so gradually they are missed. Diagnosis is straightforward with a TSH blood test, and treatment with daily levothyroxine is simple and highly effective. Routine monitoring ensures the dose stays correct over time.
precautions: Take thyroid medication consistently on empty stomach
redFlagHints: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin

diseases.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
diseases.description: Diabetic ketoacidosis is a life-threatening complication of diabetes marked by severe insulin deficiency, high blood sugar, ketone buildup and metabolic acidosis. It usually develops over hours to a day in type 1 diabetics — sometimes in undiagnosed cases — often triggered by illness, missed insulin doses or infection. Warning signs are nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, deep rapid breathing, fruity breath and eventually confusion. Urgent hospital care with IV fluids, insulin and electrolyte correction is required.
precautions: Check ketones when sick or hyperglycemic
diets: Nothing by mouth until stable; then small frequent meals
redFlagHints: Known diabetic with vomiting, abdominal pain, deep rapid breathing, fruity breath

diseases.name: Obesity
diseases.description: Obesity is defined clinically as a body mass index of 30 or higher, reflecting excess body fat that raises the risk of many diseases — type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, certain cancers, sleep apnea and joint problems. It arises from complex interactions of genetics, environment, behaviour and biology, and is not simply a matter of willpower. Treatment combines dietary changes, regular physical activity, behaviour therapy and — for many — medications like GLP-1 agonists or bariatric surgery. Even modest sustained weight loss of 5-10% improves metabolic health.
redFlagHints: BMI > 30 with multiple metabolic risk factors

diseases.name: Addison's Disease
diseases.description: Addison's disease is primary adrenal insufficiency in which the adrenal glands fail to produce enough cortisol, and often aldosterone. It develops gradually with fatigue, weight loss, low blood pressure, salt craving and characteristic skin darkening (hyperpigmentation). During physical stress — infection, injury or surgery — patients can develop a life-threatening adrenal crisis, so they must carry emergency hydrocortisone and wear a medical ID. Daily steroid replacement restores normal function and lifespan.
redFlagHints: Fatigue, weight loss, skin hyperpigmentation, low blood pressure

diseases.name: Cushing's Syndrome
diseases.description: Cushing's syndrome results from prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, most commonly from long-term corticosteroid therapy (iatrogenic) but sometimes from adrenal or pituitary tumors. Classic features include central weight gain with thin arms and legs, moon-shaped face, purple stretch marks, easy bruising and high blood pressure. Untreated it raises the risk of diabetes, osteoporosis and infection. Treatment targets the cause — tapering steroids when possible, or surgery for tumors.
medications: Ketoconazole or metyrapone in select cases
workouts: Gentle resistance training to preserve muscle
redFlagHints: Central weight gain, moon face, purple striae, easy bruising

diseases.name: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema)
diseases.description: Atopic dermatitis, commonly called eczema, is a chronic relapsing inflammatory skin condition causing very itchy, dry patches that often affect the elbows, knees, wrists and neck. It usually starts in childhood and tends to run in families along with asthma and allergic rhinitis (the 'atopic triad'). Triggers include harsh soaps, dry air, stress and certain allergens. Daily moisturising, gentle skin care and topical corticosteroids or calcineurin inhibitors control most cases, with newer biologics available for severe disease.
diets: Only eliminate foods if proven trigger
workouts: Any type; shower and moisturize after sweating
redFlagHints: Itchy dry patches, flexural distribution, personal/family atopy

diseases.name: Psoriasis
diseases.description: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune skin disease in which skin cells multiply too quickly, forming thick, silvery-scaled plaques typically on the elbows, knees, scalp and lower back. It can also affect nails and joints (psoriatic arthritis). Triggers include stress, infections, skin trauma, smoking and certain medications. Management ranges from topical treatments and phototherapy for mild disease to systemic drugs and biologics targeting specific immune pathways for moderate to severe cases.
medications: Topical corticosteroids and vitamin D analogs
redFlagHints: Well-demarcated silvery scaly plaques, nail pitting, scalp involvement

diseases.name: Contact Dermatitis
diseases.description: Contact dermatitis is an inflammatory skin reaction that develops where the skin touches an irritant or allergen. Irritant contact dermatitis is common in jobs with frequent handwashing or chemical exposure, while allergic contact dermatitis occurs in sensitised individuals to substances like nickel, fragrances, poison ivy or cosmetics. The rash is typically itchy and red in the pattern of the exposure. Identifying and avoiding the trigger, along with topical corticosteroids for flares, usually resolves the problem.
precautions: Identify and avoid trigger (metals, plants, cosmetics)
workouts: Any type; rinse sweat off promptly
redFlagHints: Rash in pattern matching exposure (watch strap, ring, poison ivy line)

diseases.name: Urticaria
diseases.description: Urticaria, commonly called hives, is a skin reaction producing itchy raised welts (wheals) caused by histamine release from mast cells. Acute urticaria is often triggered by foods, medications, infections or insect stings and resolves within six weeks. Chronic urticaria lasts longer than six weeks and is often idiopathic or autoimmune. Most cases respond to non-sedating antihistamines, sometimes at higher than usual doses; severe chronic cases may require omalizumab or short steroid courses.
precautions: Seek urgent care if swelling of face or breathing difficulty
workouts: Exercise can trigger in some; cool-down post-exercise
redFlagHints: Transient raised itchy wheals, sometimes with swelling

diseases.name: Acne Vulgaris
diseases.description: Acne is one of the most common skin conditions, developing when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells and colonised by Cutibacterium acnes bacteria. It presents as blackheads, whiteheads, inflamed pimples and sometimes deeper cysts, most often on the face, chest and back. Acne is driven by hormones, genetics and lifestyle, and typically peaks in adolescence. Gentle cleansing, topical retinoids and benzoyl peroxide control most cases, with oral antibiotics or isotretinoin reserved for severe disease.
diets: Limit high-glycemic foods and excess dairy (evidence mixed)
redFlagHints: Face/chest/back pimples and comedones, adolescent or young adult

diseases.name: Rosacea
diseases.description: Rosacea is a chronic skin condition that causes redness, visible blood vessels and sometimes pimple-like bumps on the central face. It typically starts in middle age and is more common in fair-skinned individuals. Common triggers include sun exposure, heat, spicy foods, alcohol and stress. Daily sunscreen, trigger avoidance, topical metronidazole or ivermectin and oral doxycycline (for inflammatory forms) are effective long-term controls.
precautions: Identify triggers (spicy food, alcohol, sun, heat)
redFlagHints: Central facial redness with flushing, visible vessels, papules

diseases.name: Fungal Skin Infection
diseases.description: Fungal skin infections, including ringworm (tinea corporis), athlete's foot (tinea pedis) and jock itch (tinea cruris), are caused by dermatophyte fungi that thrive in warm moist environments. They cause itchy scaly patches, often with central clearing and an advancing edge. Topical antifungal creams like clotrimazole or terbinafine for 2-4 weeks cure most localised infections. Keeping skin dry, changing socks frequently and not sharing towels prevent recurrence and spread.
medications: Oral antifungals for extensive or nail infections
redFlagHints: Itchy scaly patches, ring-shaped lesions, between-toes maceration

diseases.name: Scabies
diseases.description: Scabies is a skin infestation by the tiny mite Sarcoptes scabiei, which burrows into the upper skin layer to lay eggs. The hallmark symptom is intense itching that is worse at night, with a bumpy rash often seen in the finger webs, wrists, armpits, belt line and genitals. It spreads easily through prolonged skin-to-skin contact and within households. Treatment with permethrin 5% cream or oral ivermectin, applied to all household members simultaneously plus washing bedding and clothing in hot water, eliminates infestation.
medications: Oral ivermectin for severe or crusted cases
redFlagHints: Severe itching worse at night, rash in webs of fingers, wrists, waist

diseases.name: Herpes Zoster (Shingles)
diseases.description: Shingles is a painful rash caused by reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus that stayed dormant in nerve tissue after childhood chickenpox. The rash appears as a cluster of blisters in a band on one side of the body or face, often preceded by tingling or burning pain. Complications include postherpetic neuralgia — persistent nerve pain lasting months — and, if it involves the eye, possible vision loss. Antivirals started within 72 hours of rash onset shorten duration, and the shingles vaccine is recommended for adults over 50.
diets: Balanced diet; lysine-rich foods sometimes recommended
redFlagHints: Unilateral painful vesicular rash in a band, often with prodromal tingling

diseases.name: Impetigo
diseases.description: Impetigo is a highly contagious superficial skin infection caused most often by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes, affecting children more than adults. It typically produces red sores around the nose and mouth that quickly rupture and form honey-coloured crusts. Good hand hygiene, covering lesions and keeping fingernails short limit spread. Topical mupirocin treats localised cases, while oral antibiotics are needed for widespread or bullous impetigo.
workouts: Rest from contact activities until healed
redFlagHints: Golden-crusted sores around nose and mouth, often in children

diseases.name: Cellulitis
diseases.description: Cellulitis is a bacterial infection of the skin and soft tissue, producing a red, warm, tender and rapidly-spreading area of skin, usually on a lower limb. It typically enters through a crack, cut, insect bite or athlete's foot fissure and is most often caused by streptococci or staphylococci. Untreated it can progress to abscess, sepsis or, rarely, necrotising fasciitis. Oral antibiotics suffice for mild cases; IV antibiotics and hospitalisation are needed for severe or rapidly-progressing infections.
medications: Oral or IV antibiotics depending on severity
workouts: Elevate affected limb during acute phase
redFlagHints: Red, warm, tender, spreading skin area, often with fever

diseases.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
diseases.description: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune disease that causes symmetrical inflammation and swelling of the small joints, most commonly the hands, wrists and feet. Typical symptoms include morning stiffness lasting more than an hour, joint pain, fatigue and, over time, joint deformity if untreated. Early aggressive treatment with disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) like methotrexate, often combined with biologics, preserves joint function and substantially reduces long-term disability. Regular rheumatology follow-up and lifestyle adjustments are important.
diets: Limit red meat and ultra-processed foods
redFlagHints: Symmetric small-joint stiffness worse in the morning, over 30 minutes

diseases.name: Osteoarthritis
diseases.description: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease caused by gradual wear and loss of cartilage, most commonly affecting the knees, hips, hands and spine in adults over 50. It produces joint pain that worsens with activity and improves with rest, morning stiffness lasting under 30 minutes, reduced range of motion and sometimes joint grinding. Weight management, low-impact exercise and physical therapy are central to management, supported by simple analgesics, topical NSAIDs and targeted intra-articular injections. Joint replacement is considered when conservative measures fail.
redFlagHints: Joint pain worse with activity, stiffness under 30 minutes, older adult

diseases.name: Gout
diseases.description: Gout is a form of inflammatory arthritis caused by crystallisation of excess uric acid in the joints, classically producing sudden severe pain, redness and swelling at the base of the big toe. Attacks often come on at night and are triggered by alcohol, high-purine foods (organ meats, shellfish) or sudden dehydration. Acute flares respond to NSAIDs, colchicine or corticosteroids, while long-term urate-lowering therapy with allopurinol or febuxostat prevents recurrence. Dietary moderation also helps.
medications: Allopurinol or febuxostat for long-term lowering
diets: Limit red meat, organ meats, shellfish, beer
redFlagHints: Sudden severe pain, redness, swelling of a single joint (often big toe)

diseases.name: Fibromyalgia
diseases.description: Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition characterised by widespread musculoskeletal pain, profound fatigue, sleep disturbance and cognitive difficulties (often called 'fibro fog'). It is thought to involve altered pain processing in the central nervous system. Symptoms often fluctuate and can significantly affect quality of life. Treatment combines regular low-impact exercise, sleep hygiene, cognitive behavioural therapy and medications like duloxetine, pregabalin or low-dose amitriptyline to reduce symptom burden.
redFlagHints: Widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, tender points, often women 20-50

diseases.name: Lower Back Pain
diseases.description: Lower back pain is one of the most common complaints in primary care, typically arising from muscle strain, poor posture, prolonged sitting or a minor disc problem. Most episodes are mechanical and resolve within four to six weeks with staying active, simple analgesics and gentle core-strengthening exercises. Red flags requiring urgent evaluation include pain with fever, unexplained weight loss, history of cancer, trauma or loss of bowel/bladder control. Chronic cases benefit from physical therapy, ergonomic changes and occasionally targeted injections.
redFlagHints: Localized low back pain after lifting or prolonged sitting, improving with movement

diseases.name: Tendinitis
diseases.description: Tendinitis is inflammation of a tendon, usually from repetitive overuse — think 'tennis elbow', 'rotator cuff tendinitis' or 'Achilles tendinitis'. It causes pain, tenderness and sometimes mild swelling right at the tendon, aggravated by the activity that caused it. Treatment combines relative rest, ice, NSAIDs and a gradual progressive loading program (eccentric exercises). Recovery can take weeks to months, and resuming activity too quickly is the most common cause of setback.
redFlagHints: Pain at a specific tendon with activity, sometimes swelling

diseases.name: Sprains and Strains
diseases.description: Sprains are injuries to ligaments (the bands connecting bones), while strains affect muscles or tendons. Both typically follow a sudden twist, fall or over-stretching and produce pain, swelling, bruising and reduced movement. The RICE approach — rest, ice, compression, elevation — in the first 48-72 hours limits swelling. Gradual progressive rehabilitation restores strength and flexibility; moderate to severe sprains may benefit from formal physical therapy.
redFlagHints: Acute pain, swelling, sometimes bruising after twist or fall

diseases.name: Osteoporosis
diseases.description: Osteoporosis is a skeletal disease in which bone mineral density drops and bone architecture deteriorates, leaving bones fragile and fracture-prone. It is most common in postmenopausal women and older adults of either sex, and is typically silent until a fracture occurs — often of the hip, spine or wrist. DEXA scanning identifies at-risk patients, and treatment combines calcium and vitamin D, weight-bearing and resistance exercise, and bone-strengthening drugs like bisphosphonates or denosumab. Fall prevention is equally important.
redFlagHints: Height loss, kyphosis, fragility fracture, postmenopausal woman

diseases.name: Sciatica
diseases.description: Sciatica is pain that radiates along the sciatic nerve — from the lower back down the buttock and the back of the leg, often below the knee. The usual cause is a herniated lumbar disc compressing the nerve root, though spinal stenosis and piriformis syndrome can also produce similar symptoms. Most cases improve within six weeks with staying active (not strict bed rest), NSAIDs and targeted physiotherapy. Persistent pain, significant weakness or bowel/bladder symptoms warrant imaging and possible surgical evaluation.
medications: Short oral steroids in select cases
redFlagHints: Low back pain radiating down one leg, worse with sitting or coughing

diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection
diseases.description: A urinary tract infection is a bacterial infection anywhere in the urinary tract, but most commonly the bladder (cystitis). It typically causes burning on urination, frequency, urgency, lower abdominal discomfort and sometimes cloudy or blood-tinged urine. UTIs are especially common in women because of a shorter urethra. A short course of oral antibiotics like nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole cures most cases quickly; prompt treatment prevents upward spread to the kidneys.
redFlagHints: Burning on urination, frequency, urgency, cloudy urine

diseases.name: Kidney Stones
diseases.description: Kidney stones are hard deposits of minerals and salts that form in the kidneys, most commonly calcium oxalate. When a stone tries to pass through the ureter it can cause sudden severe flank pain that radiates to the groin (renal colic), often with nausea, vomiting and blood in the urine. Small stones usually pass on their own with fluids and pain control, sometimes aided by alpha-blockers like tamsulosin. Larger or obstructing stones may need lithotripsy or endoscopic removal, and long-term prevention focuses on hydration and dietary adjustments.
diets: Limit oxalate-rich foods if calcium oxalate stones
redFlagHints: Severe flank pain radiating to groin, hematuria, nausea

diseases.name: Acute Kidney Injury
diseases.description: Acute kidney injury is a sudden drop in kidney function measured in hours to days, often reversible when recognised and treated early. Causes fall into three groups: reduced blood flow (dehydration, blood loss), direct kidney damage (drugs, toxins, glomerulonephritis) and obstruction (enlarged prostate, stones). Warning signs include reduced urine output, swelling, nausea and confusion. Treatment addresses the cause, stops nephrotoxic drugs and supports the patient through recovery; severe cases may require temporary dialysis.
diets: Restrict sodium, potassium, phosphorus as advised
redFlagHints: Reduced urine output, swelling, fatigue, recent illness or medication start

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
diseases.description: Chronic kidney disease is a progressive long-term loss of kidney function, most commonly caused by diabetes and hypertension. Early disease is usually silent, detected only by blood tests (creatinine, estimated GFR) and urine tests (albumin). As disease advances, patients develop fatigue, anaemia, fluid retention and electrolyte disturbances. Management focuses on tight BP and glucose control, newer agents like SGLT2 inhibitors that protect the kidney, and avoiding nephrotoxic drugs; advanced disease may require dialysis or transplantation.
diets: Limit potassium and phosphorus if advanced
redFlagHints: Fatigue, swelling, nausea, itching, often diabetic or hypertensive

diseases.name: Pyelonephritis
diseases.description: Pyelonephritis is an infection of the upper urinary tract that involves the kidney itself, usually from bacteria ascending from a lower UTI. Typical features are high fever with chills, flank pain, nausea and vomiting, often with urinary symptoms. Untreated it can cause bacteremia, sepsis or scarring of the kidney. Most cases need at least oral antibiotics like fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins; severe cases require hospitalisation for IV antibiotics and fluids.
redFlagHints: Flank pain, fever, chills, nausea, urinary symptoms

diseases.name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
diseases.description: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is a common non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate gland in men, especially after age 50. As the prostate grows it can compress the urethra and cause troublesome lower urinary tract symptoms — weak stream, hesitancy, nocturia, incomplete emptying and urgency. Alpha-blockers (tamsulosin) relax bladder-neck muscle quickly, while 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride) shrink the gland over months. Persistent or severe cases may benefit from minimally invasive procedures or surgery.
redFlagHints: Older man, weak stream, urinary frequency, nocturia, incomplete emptying

diseases.name: Urinary Incontinence
diseases.description: Urinary incontinence is the involuntary leakage of urine. The main types are stress incontinence (leakage with coughing or lifting), urge incontinence (sudden uncontrollable need), overflow incontinence and mixed forms. It is more common in women after childbirth and in older adults of both sexes, though not a normal part of aging. Pelvic floor exercises, bladder training, weight management and targeted medications — antimuscarinics, mirabegron or topical estrogen — help most patients, with surgical options for refractory stress incontinence.
redFlagHints: Involuntary urine leakage with activity, urgency, or overflow

diseases.name: Primary Dysmenorrhea
diseases.description: Primary dysmenorrhea refers to painful menstrual cramps that occur in otherwise normal pelvic anatomy, caused by prostaglandin-driven uterine contractions. Pain typically begins a few hours before or at the start of menstruation and lasts 1-3 days, sometimes with nausea, fatigue and diarrhoea. NSAIDs started at the first sign of pain are the most effective relief, and combined oral contraceptives reduce both pain and flow. Heat, regular aerobic exercise and anti-inflammatory foods may also help.
precautions: Heat and rest during painful days
