redFlagHints: Lower abdominal cramping with menstruation, sometimes with nausea

diseases.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
diseases.description: Polycystic ovary syndrome is a common hormonal disorder in reproductive-aged women, characterised by irregular periods, signs of excess androgens (acne, hirsutism, scalp hair loss) and — on ultrasound — multiple small ovarian follicles. It is strongly associated with insulin resistance and raises long-term risk of type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome and endometrial cancer. Management is tailored to individual goals: combined oral contraceptives regulate cycles, metformin improves insulin resistance, and letrozole helps with fertility. Weight management significantly improves symptoms.
precautions: Screen for diabetes and lipid abnormalities
redFlagHints: Irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, difficulty with weight or fertility

diseases.name: Endometriosis
diseases.description: Endometriosis is a chronic gynecological condition in which endometrial-like tissue grows outside the uterus, most often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes and pelvic peritoneum. It commonly causes severe menstrual pain, deep pelvic pain with intercourse, chronic pelvic pain and infertility. Diagnosis is often delayed by years because symptoms overlap with other conditions. Treatment ranges from NSAIDs and hormonal therapy (combined pills, progestins, GnRH analogs) for pain control to laparoscopic surgery for refractory cases or fertility.
redFlagHints: Severe menstrual pain, pain with intercourse, infertility, pelvic pain

diseases.name: Ectopic Pregnancy
diseases.description: Ectopic pregnancy occurs when a fertilised egg implants outside the uterus, most often in a fallopian tube. It is a life-threatening emergency because the growing pregnancy can rupture the tube and cause massive internal bleeding. Warning signs in a pregnant woman are one-sided pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding and sometimes shoulder-tip pain from diaphragmatic irritation. Early detection by ultrasound and beta-hCG allows either medical treatment with methotrexate or surgical removal, preserving the woman's future fertility when possible.
precautions: Urgent medical evaluation for any pregnant woman with abdominal pain or bleeding
workouts: Rest and gradual return after treatment
redFlagHints: Pregnancy with one-sided pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, sometimes shoulder-tip pain

diseases.name: Uterine Fibroids
diseases.description: Uterine fibroids are non-cancerous smooth-muscle tumors of the uterus that affect a large proportion of women by age 50. Many are asymptomatic, but larger fibroids can cause heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding, pelvic pressure, urinary frequency, and subfertility. Management depends on symptoms and fertility goals, ranging from watchful waiting and iron supplementation to hormonal medications, uterine artery embolisation, myomectomy and, in some cases, hysterectomy. Most fibroids shrink after menopause.
redFlagHints: Heavy prolonged periods, pelvic pressure, reproductive-age woman

diseases.name: Menopausal Syndrome
diseases.description: Menopause is the natural cessation of menstrual periods for 12 consecutive months, typically occurring between ages 45 and 55 as ovarian estrogen production declines. The transition can bring hot flashes, night sweats, sleep disturbance, vaginal dryness and mood changes, with long-term effects on bone and cardiovascular health. Lifestyle measures (regular exercise, weight management, adequate calcium and vitamin D) help; symptomatic women may benefit from hormone therapy, SSRIs or topical estrogen for vaginal symptoms. Routine screening for osteoporosis becomes important.
redFlagHints: Hot flashes, night sweats, irregular or absent periods in women 45-55

diseases.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
diseases.description: Generalized anxiety disorder is a common mental health condition characterised by persistent and excessive worry about everyday concerns lasting six months or more, along with physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, poor sleep and difficulty concentrating. It frequently coexists with depression and can significantly impair work and relationships. First-line treatment is cognitive behavioural therapy, often combined with SSRIs or SNRIs. Reducing caffeine, regular exercise, mindfulness practice and adequate sleep form the foundation of self-management.
redFlagHints: Persistent worry for 6+ months, restlessness, sleep disturbance, muscle tension

diseases.name: Major Depressive Disorder
diseases.description: Major depressive disorder is a mental health condition in which low mood, loss of interest or pleasure and related symptoms persist for at least two weeks and interfere significantly with daily life. Additional features include sleep and appetite changes, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness and difficulty concentrating, with some people experiencing suicidal thoughts. Treatment typically combines psychotherapy (CBT, interpersonal therapy) with antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs), tailored to severity. Exercise, social connection and screening for suicide risk are integral to care.
workouts: Regular aerobic exercise has antidepressant effect
redFlagHints: Low mood most of day for 2+ weeks, anhedonia, sleep/appetite changes, hopelessness

diseases.name: Panic Disorder
diseases.description: Panic disorder is characterised by recurrent unexpected panic attacks — sudden intense surges of fear with physical symptoms like palpitations, sweating, breathlessness, trembling and a sense of impending doom — usually peaking within 10 minutes. Between attacks, people often fear recurrence, and some begin avoiding places associated with past episodes (agoraphobia). Cognitive behavioural therapy focused on interoceptive exposure is highly effective, often combined with SSRIs. Benzodiazepines have a limited role due to dependence risk.
workouts: Regular aerobic exercise reduces attack frequency
redFlagHints: Sudden intense fear with palpitations, sweating, breathlessness, dizziness, often under 10 min

diseases.name: Insomnia Disorder
diseases.description: Insomnia disorder is persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or waking too early despite adequate opportunity to sleep, occurring at least three nights a week for three or more months. Daytime consequences include fatigue, poor concentration, irritability and impaired performance. Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the first-line treatment — more effective and durable than sleep medications. When medications are used, short courses of melatonin, doxepin or specific hypnotics are preferred over long-term benzodiazepines.
medications: Short-term melatonin, zolpidem, or doxepin in select cases
diets: Avoid heavy meals and alcohol before bed
workouts: Regular exercise (not too close to bedtime)
redFlagHints: Difficulty falling or staying asleep 3+ nights weekly for 3+ months

diseases.name: Burnout Syndrome
diseases.description: Burnout is a state of emotional, physical and mental exhaustion caused by prolonged and excessive workplace stress. The classic triad is feelings of depletion, increased mental distance from one's work (cynicism) and reduced professional efficacy. It affects performance, relationships and physical health, increasing risk of depression, anxiety and cardiovascular disease. Recovery usually requires a combination of workplace changes, protected recovery time, reconnecting with social and personal life, and addressing any co-existing mental health conditions.
redFlagHints: Exhaustion, cynicism, reduced professional efficacy, work-related

diseases.name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
diseases.description: PTSD can develop after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence. Core features are intrusive memories or nightmares of the trauma, active avoidance of reminders, negative changes in thoughts and mood, and hyperarousal symptoms like being easily startled or sleeping poorly. Evidence-based trauma-focused psychotherapies (prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, EMDR) are the most effective treatments, often paired with SSRIs and support for co-existing conditions. Self-medication with alcohol or drugs worsens outcomes and should be avoided.
redFlagHints: Flashbacks, nightmares, hypervigilance after trauma exposure

diseases.name: Allergic Rhinitis
diseases.description: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) is an inflammatory nasal condition triggered by an IgE-mediated response to inhaled allergens like pollen, dust mites, mold or pet dander. It produces sneezing, itchy nose and eyes, clear runny nose and congestion, either seasonally or year-round. Impact on sleep, concentration and quality of life is often underestimated. Trigger avoidance, intranasal corticosteroids, non-sedating antihistamines and — for persistent cases — allergen immunotherapy are the mainstays of treatment.
precautions: Close windows during high pollen days
diets: No specific diet; identify any food-pollen cross-reactions
redFlagHints: Seasonal or perennial sneezing, itchy nose/eyes, clear runny nose

diseases.name: Anaphylaxis
diseases.description: Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening systemic allergic reaction that develops within minutes of exposure to a trigger like peanuts, tree nuts, shellfish, bee stings or medications. It produces a combination of skin symptoms (hives, lip/tongue swelling), airway narrowing, breathing difficulty and sometimes shock. Intramuscular epinephrine to the outer thigh is the single most important treatment and should be given at the first sign — never delayed for antihistamines. Patients with known triggers should carry two auto-injectors and wear medical ID.
workouts: Exercise-induced anaphylaxis: avoid known food triggers before exercise
redFlagHints: Sudden widespread hives, lip/tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, hypotension after exposure

diseases.name: Food Allergy
diseases.description: A food allergy is an immune-mediated reaction to specific food proteins, distinct from food intolerance. Most true allergies produce symptoms within minutes to two hours — hives, lip/tongue swelling, vomiting, wheezing — and can progress to anaphylaxis. The most common triggers are peanuts, tree nuts, milk, egg, soy, wheat, fish and shellfish. Strict avoidance is currently the mainstay, while carrying epinephrine, reading labels carefully and educating family and caregivers are essential. Oral immunotherapy programs are an emerging option for select patients.
workouts: Any; caution with exercise-induced food-dependent anaphylaxis
redFlagHints: Hives, swelling, vomiting, or breathing issues after specific food

diseases.name: Angioedema
diseases.description: Angioedema is rapid-onset swelling of the deeper layers of the skin, often around the eyes, lips, tongue and sometimes the airway. It can be histamine-mediated (often with hives) or bradykinin-mediated, the latter including hereditary angioedema and ACE-inhibitor-induced cases. Treatment differs: histaminergic cases respond to antihistamines, corticosteroids and epinephrine if severe, while bradykinin-mediated angioedema needs specific agents like icatibant or C1-inhibitor concentrate. Any tongue or airway swelling is a medical emergency.
medications: Icatibant or C1-inhibitor for hereditary angioedema
redFlagHints: Swelling of lips, tongue, eyelids, sometimes airway involvement

diseases.name: Drug Allergy
diseases.description: A drug allergy is an adverse immune-mediated reaction to a medication, most commonly with penicillins and sulfa drugs. Reactions can range from mild rash to severe delayed skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and anaphylaxis. Discontinuation of the offending drug is essential, and future exposures should be avoided or carefully tested. A documented drug allergy in the medical record helps prevent re-exposure; formal drug allergy testing and sometimes desensitisation are options for critical medications.
precautions: Document allergy in records and medical ID
redFlagHints: Rash, swelling, or systemic symptoms after starting new medication

diseases.name: Otitis Media
diseases.description: Otitis media is infection or inflammation of the middle ear, most common in children because of their shorter, more horizontal eustachian tubes. It typically follows an upper respiratory infection and produces ear pain, fever and irritability in children, or reduced hearing and pressure sensation in adults. Most cases resolve within a few days with analgesics; antibiotics are used for bilateral infection in young children, severe symptoms or perforated eardrums. Repeated infections may prompt evaluation for tympanostomy tubes.
precautions: Keep ears dry if perforated eardrum
diets: Soft foods if pain with chewing
redFlagHints: Ear pain, sometimes with fever, often after a cold

diseases.name: Otitis Externa
diseases.description: Otitis externa, or swimmer's ear, is an infection of the outer ear canal that follows water retention, trauma from cotton swabs or eczema. It causes ear pain (worse with tragal pressure), itching, canal swelling and sometimes discharge. Topical antibiotic-corticosteroid ear drops treat most cases within a week. Keeping the ear dry, avoiding cotton swabs and using ear plugs while swimming prevent recurrence.
redFlagHints: Ear pain worse with tragus pressure, itching, discharge

diseases.name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
diseases.description: BPPV is the most common cause of vertigo, resulting from loose calcium carbonate crystals (otoconia) moving within the inner ear's semicircular canals. It produces brief episodes of intense spinning triggered by specific head movements — rolling over, looking up, lying down — lasting less than a minute. Hearing is normal, which helps distinguish it from Ménière's disease and labyrinthitis. Particle-repositioning manoeuvres like the Epley, typically performed by a trained clinician, resolve most cases with a single session.
redFlagHints: Brief spinning sensation with head turns or rolling over, no hearing change

diseases.name: Labyrinthitis
diseases.description: Labyrinthitis is inflammation of the inner ear (both cochlea and vestibular structures), usually following a viral illness. It causes sudden severe vertigo, imbalance and often new hearing changes or tinnitus on the affected side, with nausea and vomiting common in the first days. Symptoms improve over one to two weeks, though subtle balance issues may linger for a month. Vestibular suppressants like meclizine help acute symptoms, and vestibular rehabilitation therapy speeds long-term recovery.
redFlagHints: Vertigo with hearing changes or tinnitus, often after viral illness

diseases.name: Conjunctivitis
diseases.description: Conjunctivitis (pink eye) is inflammation of the thin membrane covering the white of the eye and inner eyelid. It has three main causes: viral (watery discharge, often with a cold), bacterial (sticky yellow-green discharge) and allergic (itching and watery discharge, usually bilateral). Viral and allergic forms are self-limited but highly contagious in the case of viral. Good hand hygiene, discarding contacts and makeup, and targeted treatment — antihistamine drops or bacterial antibiotics only when needed — resolve most episodes.
redFlagHints: Red itchy watery eyes, sometimes with discharge, contagious or allergen exposure

diseases.name: Hordeolum (Stye)
diseases.description: A stye is a tender red lump on the eyelid from an acute bacterial infection of an eyelash follicle or small eyelid gland. It usually points outward (external stye) and typically resolves within a week with warm compresses applied several times a day. Topical antibiotic ointment may speed recovery if a secondary infection develops, but oral antibiotics are rarely needed. Styes should not be squeezed, as this can spread infection.
precautions: Don't wear contacts or eye makeup
medications: Topical antibiotic ointment in select cases
redFlagHints: Painful red lump on eyelid margin

diseases.name: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
diseases.description: Acute angle-closure glaucoma is an ophthalmic emergency where the drainage angle of the eye becomes suddenly blocked, causing a rapid rise in intraocular pressure. It presents with severe one-sided eye pain, blurred vision, halos around lights, a red eye with a mid-dilated non-reactive pupil and often nausea and vomiting. Without urgent pressure-lowering treatment and peripheral iridotomy, permanent vision loss can occur within hours. Any sudden eye pain with vision change needs immediate evaluation.
redFlagHints: Severe eye pain, blurred vision, halos around lights, nausea, red eye

diseases.name: Dry Eye Syndrome
diseases.description: Dry eye syndrome is a chronic condition caused by inadequate tear production or unstable tear film, producing gritty, burning discomfort, fluctuating vision and sometimes paradoxical watering. It is common with aging, long screen use, contact lens wear, certain medications and autoimmune conditions like Sjögren's. Artificial tears, warm compresses, omega-3 supplementation, humidifiers and regular screen breaks form the base of treatment, with prescription drops like cyclosporine for more significant cases. Identifying and treating any underlying condition is key.
redFlagHints: Gritty, burning eyes worse at end of day, computer use

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.description: Iron deficiency anemia is the most common form of anemia worldwide, caused by inadequate iron intake, poor absorption (e.g., celiac disease) or chronic blood loss (menstruation, GI bleeding). It produces fatigue, pale skin, shortness of breath, brittle nails and restless legs. Treatment combines finding the underlying cause with oral iron supplementation, taken on an empty stomach with vitamin C for absorption; IV iron is reserved for intolerance or severe cases. Any new iron deficiency in postmenopausal women or men warrants a search for GI blood loss.
precautions: Take iron with vitamin C, away from calcium
medications: IV iron if intolerant or severe
diets: Iron-rich foods (lean red meat, lentils, leafy greens)
redFlagHints: Fatigue, pale skin, brittle nails, heavy periods or GI bleeding

diseases.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
diseases.description: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes a large-cell (macrocytic) anemia and can produce neurological symptoms that are sometimes irreversible if untreated — numbness, tingling, weakness, balance problems and memory changes. At-risk groups include strict vegans, older adults, patients with pernicious anemia (autoimmune loss of intrinsic factor) and those who have had gastric bypass. Oral cobalamin or intramuscular injections correct the deficiency; neurological changes respond best when treatment is started early.
precautions: Screen at-risk patients (vegans, older adults, post-gastric surgery)
diets: Meat, fish, dairy, eggs; fortified foods for vegans
redFlagHints: Fatigue, pale skin, tingling hands/feet, balance problems, vegan diet or pernicious anemia

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia
diseases.description: Thrombocytopenia is a platelet count below normal, which raises bleeding risk. Causes fall into three categories: reduced production (bone marrow disease, viral infection, drug effects), increased destruction (ITP, DIC, TTP) and sequestration (enlarged spleen). Features include easy bruising, tiny red dots on the skin (petechiae), mucosal bleeding and, when severe, internal bleeding. Treatment depends on cause and severity — stopping offending drugs, steroids or IVIG for ITP, and platelet transfusions for life-threatening bleeding.
medications: Depends on cause (steroids, IVIG, TPO agonists)
workouts: Avoid contact sports until platelets adequate
redFlagHints: Easy bruising, petechiae, mucosal bleeding, heavy menstrual bleeding

diseases.name: Sickle Cell Disease
diseases.description: Sickle cell disease is an inherited red blood cell disorder in which hemoglobin S distorts red cells into sickle shapes under stress, blocking small blood vessels. Patients experience recurrent painful vaso-occlusive crises, anemia, infection susceptibility and chronic organ damage over time. Triggers include dehydration, cold, high altitude and infection. Hydroxyurea reduces crises, newer agents like voxelotor and crizanlizumab add options, and allogeneic stem cell transplant is curative in selected patients.
redFlagHints: Severe pain episodes, chest pain, splenic issues, family history

diseases.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
diseases.description: Vitamin D deficiency is common, especially in people with limited sun exposure, darker skin, older age or malabsorption. Mild deficiency is often asymptomatic but can cause fatigue, muscle weakness and bone pain; severe or long-standing deficiency contributes to osteoporosis and, in extreme cases, osteomalacia. Treatment is straightforward supplementation with vitamin D3 at doses guided by the severity of deficiency, often combined with adequate calcium. Sensible sun exposure and dietary sources (oily fish, fortified foods) help maintain levels.
redFlagHints: Bone pain, muscle weakness, fatigue, limited sun exposure

diseases.name: Dehydration
diseases.description: Dehydration is a state in which body water loss exceeds intake, disturbing electrolyte balance and impairing cellular function. Common triggers include vomiting, diarrhoea, heavy sweating in heat, diuretic use and inadequate fluid intake, especially in older adults and young children. Early signs include thirst, dry mouth, headache and dark urine; severe dehydration causes dizziness, confusion, rapid heart rate and fainting. Oral rehydration solutions work well for mild-to-moderate dehydration, while severe cases need IV fluids.
precautions: Replace electrolytes during illness or heavy sweating
workouts: Hydrate before, during, and after activity
redFlagHints: Dry mouth, reduced urine, dizziness, dark urine, recent illness or heat

diseases.name: Heat Exhaustion
diseases.description: Heat exhaustion is a heat-related illness that develops when the body cannot cool itself adequately in hot environments, usually after prolonged exertion. It features heavy sweating, weakness, nausea, headache, dizziness and muscle cramps, with a rising core temperature that is not yet dangerously high. Moving to a cool environment, loosening clothing, rehydrating and cooling the body actively usually resolve symptoms within hours. If left untreated, it can progress to heat stroke, which is life-threatening.
redFlagHints: Heavy sweating, weakness, headache, nausea after heat exposure

diseases.name: Heat Stroke
diseases.description: Heat stroke is a life-threatening emergency defined by a core body temperature above 40°C combined with neurological dysfunction — confusion, slurred speech, agitation, seizure or loss of consciousness. The skin may be either hot and dry or sweaty depending on the type. Every minute counts: call emergency services and begin active cooling immediately with cold-water immersion or continuous soaking and fanning. Delayed treatment dramatically increases mortality and risk of permanent organ damage.
redFlagHints: High body temperature, confusion, hot dry skin (or still sweating), loss of consciousness

diseases.name: Hypothermia
diseases.description: Hypothermia occurs when core body temperature drops below 35°C, most often from prolonged cold exposure, especially in older adults, infants, and people who are wet, intoxicated or have inadequate shelter. Early features include shivering, slurred speech and confusion; severe hypothermia can cause loss of consciousness, arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Treatment involves gentle rewarming — removing wet clothes, insulating with dry blankets, warm fluids if alert — with severe cases needing hospital-based active rewarming. Alcohol and vigorous external rubbing should be avoided.
redFlagHints: Shivering, confusion, slurred speech, slow breathing after cold exposure

diseases.name: Breast Cancer Warning Signs
diseases.description: This entry describes a warning-sign pattern rather than a specific diagnosis. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, and early detection dramatically improves outcomes. Warning features that warrant urgent specialist evaluation include a new breast lump, nipple discharge (especially bloody), skin dimpling or redness, nipple inversion or a lump in the armpit. None of these symptoms confirm cancer, but any of them should prompt clinical examination and appropriate imaging (mammography, ultrasound or MRI). Routine age-appropriate screening saves lives.
redFlagHints: New breast lump, nipple discharge, skin changes, axillary lump

diseases.name: Colorectal Cancer Warning Signs
diseases.description: This entry describes a warning-sign pattern rather than a confirmed diagnosis. Colorectal cancer is one of the most common cancers and is highly preventable with screening. Warning signs that warrant urgent evaluation include a persistent change in bowel habits, blood in stool, unexplained weight loss, iron-deficiency anaemia in a man or postmenopausal woman, and persistent abdominal pain. Colonoscopy confirms the diagnosis and can remove precancerous polyps. A high-fibre diet, limiting red and processed meats, physical activity and regular age-appropriate screening substantially reduce risk.
redFlagHints: Persistent change in bowel habits, blood in stool, unexplained weight loss, iron deficiency

diseases.name: Lung Cancer Warning Signs
diseases.description: This entry describes a warning-sign pattern rather than a specific diagnosis. Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, with smoking as the dominant risk factor. Concerning symptoms include a cough lasting more than three weeks, coughing up blood, unexplained weight loss, chest pain and persistent breathlessness, especially in current or former smokers. Prompt imaging and specialist referral are essential, and low-dose CT screening is recommended for high-risk individuals. Smoking cessation remains the single most effective preventive measure.
redFlagHints: Persistent cough over 3 weeks, hemoptysis, weight loss, heavy smoking history

diseases.name: Skin Cancer Warning Signs (Melanoma)
diseases.description: This entry describes a warning-sign pattern rather than a specific diagnosis. Melanoma is the most dangerous type of skin cancer but is highly curable when caught early. The ABCDE checklist helps evaluate suspicious moles — Asymmetry, irregular Border, varied Colour, Diameter larger than 6 mm and any Evolution in shape, size or symptoms. Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen, avoiding peak-UV sun exposure, regular self-exams and annual dermatology visits (especially with many moles or family history) substantially reduce risk and enable early diagnosis.
precautions: Annual dermatologist visit if risk factors
redFlagHints: Mole with ABCDE features — Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, Diameter >6mm, Evolution
